story.title: Four Decades After Its First Lecture, Sultan Qaboos University Reflects on Forty Years of Building Minds

detail.extracted_title: Four Decades After Its First Lecture, Sultan Qaboos University Reflects on Forty Years of Building Minds
detail.excerpt: Inside the Grand Hall at Al Khoudh, generations of professors, graduates, and current students gathered under the theme "Extended Impact" to mark forty years since Oman opened its first national university.
detail.article_html:
In the Grand Hall of the Sultan Qaboos University Cultural Center, the faces in the rows tell the timeline of modern Oman better than any plaque on the wall. Former university presidents sit beside young undergraduates who were born decades after the first lectures began in 1986. Engineers, physicians, teachers, and researchers who once walked the shaded walkways of Al Khoudh with textbooks under their arms have returned as leaders of ministries, laboratories, and classrooms across the country.

Yesterday, His Highness Sayyid Theyazin bin Haitham Al Said, Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, presided over the ceremony marking the fortieth anniversary of the opening of Sultan Qaboos University. Held under the theme "Extended Impact" (Athar Mumtadd), the gathering looked back at the autumn forty years ago when Oman's first national university opened its doors, while turning its focus toward the fifth decade now beginning.

Beginning With the Human Mind

Speaking before the assembly, His Highness Sayyid Dr. Fahad bin Al Julanda Al Said, Vice Chancellor of Sultan Qaboos University, returned to the founding principle that brought the campus into existence. The idea took shape in 1980, when the late Sultan Qaboos bin Said set in motion a national institution built on a clear conviction: that the essential starting point for building a country is building its people.

When the university welcomed its first cohort six years later, it inaugurated a new era of scientific training and intellectual self-reliance in the Sultanate. For families in wilayats from Musandam to Dhofar, sending a son or daughter to the valley of Al Khoudh meant watching local talent step into medicine, agriculture, engineering, science, and the humanities at home.

During yesterday's ceremony, Sayyid Fahad noted that the university's work never stayed confined within lecture halls. Its graduates carried what they learned into every governorate, while studies conducted in its laboratories helped shape national development plans. Guided today by the priorities of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, who has placed education and scientific research at the forefront of the Renewed Renaissance, the university has linked its academic programs, research centers, and partnerships directly to the knowledge economy goals of Oman Vision 2040.

Memory in Documentary, Verse, and Postage Stamps

The anniversary program wove archival records together with the voices of the current generation. A documentary film titled Beyond Forty (Ab'ad Min Arba'een) traced the university's path from the initial 1980 vision to its present-day research centers, pairing historical documents with personal memories of how the campus shaped minds and communities across four decades.

Two current students, Ahmed bin Butti Al Shukaili and Al Jawhara bint Salim Al Hosni, took the stage to recite The Luster of Forty (Bareeq Al Arba'een), a poem written for the occasion by poet Dr. Said bin Mohammed Al Maktoumi.

To preserve the milestone in Oman's material archive, His Highness Sayyid Theyazin launched a commemorative postal issue marking the fortieth anniversary of the university's opening. The release brings together four stamps in a single unified art sheet alongside a souvenir card and a first-day cover stamped with the official anniversary postmark, illustrating forty years of human development, knowledge production, and future foresight.

Looking Into the Fifth Decade

Following the ceremony, Sayyid Theyazin toured the accompanying exhibition, Forty Years of Impact, structured around three thematic pillars: Building: Vision and Growth, Impact: Extended Giving, and The Future: Shaping Tomorrow. The displays trace how scholarly work on campus has moved beyond theoretical papers into applied research partnerships, innovation programs, and policy solutions serving Omani institutions.

Today, by Royal directive of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, the university is hosting a two-day scientific symposium examining four decades of economic, social, and scientific contributions across Oman. As Sultan Qaboos University steps into its fifth decade, it treats the past forty years as a foundation for the next generation of Omani thinkers, builders, and researchers.

detail.instagram_caption:
In the Grand Hall of the Sultan Qaboos University Cultural Center in Al Khoudh, four decades of Omani higher education came together under one roof. Presided over by His Highness Sayyid Theyazin bin Haitham Al Said, Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, the ceremony marked the fortieth anniversary of the opening of Sultan Qaboos University under the theme "Extended Impact" (Athar Mumtadd).

Speaking at the celebration, His Highness Sayyid Dr. Fahad bin Al Julanda Al Said, Vice Chancellor of the university, reflected on the 1980 vision of the late Sultan Qaboos bin Said, who founded Oman's first national university on the principle that building a nation begins with building its people. Over the past forty years, graduates from every wilayat have stepped from the walkways of Al Khoudh into leadership across medicine, engineering, education, science, and public service, while guided today by His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tariq's focus on scientific research and the knowledge economy of Oman Vision 2040.

During the ceremony, Sayyid Theyazin launched a commemorative four-stamp postal issue and first-day cover documenting four decades of academic and national contribution, followed by a tour of the "Forty Years of Impact" exhibition and the start of a two-day scientific symposium held by Royal directive.
